discriminatorUsedAndWhyItSurvivesTheOver: assessed_value presence (via the existing nonNegativeDollarOrNull coercion), on a row already scoped to the declared vintage by fetchCountyCadPropertyRoll's own WHERE tax_year = declared.taxYear. Verified in code, not assumed: lib/cad-ingest/src/txgio/landuse.ts hard-codes assessedValue: null on every row the StratMap adapter produces (it structurally cannot populate this field); lib/cad-ingest/src/p78Merge.ts's applyPathAMerge unconditionally overwrites sourceFile/sourceVintage on every ON CONFLICT merge (out.sourceFile = inc.sourceFile, never coalesced) but COALESCEs assessedValue (coalesce(incoming, existing) -- a genuine CAD import's assessed value therefore survives a later StratMap merge at the same declared tax year even though source_file does not). This is the same discriminator CTX-HAYS-SPLIT already validated and used to recover 244 genuine CAD rows from under an overwritten StratMap source tag (_inbox/2026-09-09_ctx-hays-split_close.json).
a3_optionTakenAndWhy: Exempted the serve guard (refusePayloadAtServe in serveGuards.ts) for a well-formed earned retirement (isEarnedRecordRetirement(payload.recordRetirement)), rather than nulling the retired payload's situs at bake time. Reason: situsForRetiredBake (nodeFacetBakeTier1ConformantCli.ts) already deliberately preserves the raw last-known claim value even when punctuation-only, by explicit prior design comment ('an honest retirement declaration must not depend on whether the stale claim happens to carry a well-formed address') -- nulling it would reverse that already-deliberate CTX-RETIRE decision, destroying real (if messy) last-known-claim information for every retired account with a marginal situs. recordRetirement is already present on every conformant payload with a well-formed-object guard, and refusePayloadAtServe already receives the full payload including that field, so the exemption is additive and does not weaken the guard for any on-roll (non-retired) claim -- CTX-SITUS-SKIP's own guard is completely untouched, proven by a dedicated test.

lessons: assessed_value presence, not source_file, is the durable per-row lineage discriminator across any merge shape that uses p78Merge.ts's applyPathAMerge -- it survives ON CONFLICT because it is COALESCE-merged, while source_file/source_vintage are unconditional overwrites. This is the second lane (after CTX-HAYS-SPLIT) to rely on this; if a third county-lineage question comes up, this is now a load-bearing, twice-validated pattern, not a one-off.

A module that asserts an environment precondition (DATABASE_URL) at plain module-load time, not call time, silently makes every future importer of anything in that module inherit the precondition -- including a light, unrelated utility that happens to need one type/function from it. Before importing into a light module, check what the source module's OWN unmodified test does when run standalone with no env configured; if it fails to load, extract rather than import.

A test fixture can encode the exact defect a later dispatch is asked to fix (cadRollValue.test.ts's own first test asserted the pre-fix, wrong valueBasis). Fixing the production code without re-reading every fixture that exercises the changed function would have left a self-contradicting test suite (new tests correct, old test still asserting the bug) -- worth an explicit pass over a changed function's full existing test file, not just adding new tests alongside it.
